reasons: Classification is correct: the 180-day non-renewal notice window is double the 90-day walk-away threshold and far outside the ≤60-day fallback, so the clause fails the fallback on a material term and is properly a deviation rather than an acceptable fallback.

The redline is valid and actionable: it sets the window to 30 days (preferred), preserves the acceptable 12-month renewal term, and adds the preferred 60-day Vendor renewal reminder; the deterministic notice-window check confirms 30 days.
The pricing limb is correctly assessed as already at the preferred position (§ 8.3 caps uplift at lesser of CPI and 3%), and the finding does not re-flag it — no double-counting or over-flagging.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural with the required prefix, states what changed and why, and offers the 60-day fallback.

The failed minimal-edit heuristic (0.630) is explained by the sentence-level rewrite needed to change the notice trigger plus the added reminder sentence drawn directly from the preferred position; no unrelated terms were altered.
Severity raised to high because the drafted window sits squarely in walk-away territory (180 days vs. the 90-day threshold).
